ICSA-23-193-01.title: Rockwell Automation ControlLogix Communication Modules
ICSA-23-193-01.description: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow malicious actors to gain remote access to the running memory of the module and perform malicious activity.
recommendations: Update firmware to version 33.011 or later.
Restrict CIP traffic to known authorized devices.
Use application-layer firewalls for CIP protocol inspection.
Implement network segmentation between IT and OT.

ICSA-22-174-03.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7 Communication Processors
ICSA-22-174-03.description: A vulnerability in Siemens SIMATIC S7 communication processors could allow an unauthenticated attacker to crash the device or gain code execution by sending specially crafted S7 protocol packets.
recommendations: Apply Siemens security updates SSA-838121.
Restrict S7 protocol access to authorized engineering stations.
Enable access protection features on S7 CPUs.
Monitor for anomalous S7 traffic patterns.

ICSA-21-287-03.title: Schneider Electric EcoStruxure and Modicon
ICSA-21-287-03.description: Multiple vulnerabilities in Schneider Electric Modicon controllers could allow remote code execution, denial of service, or unauthorized access to the PLC. Exploitable via Modbus TCP without authentication.
recommendations: Apply Schneider Electric patches SEVD-2021-285-01.
Enable Modbus TCP security features where available.
Deploy firewalls with Modbus deep packet inspection.
Restrict Modbus port 502 access to authorized HMIs only.
Implement network monitoring for anomalous Modbus traffic.

ICSA-24-030-01.title: SEL Real Time Automation Controller (RTAC)
ICSA-24-030-01.description: Vulnerabilities in SEL RTAC products could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands on the device. RTACs are widely used in electric utility substations.
recommendations: Update to the latest RTAC firmware version.
Restrict web interface access to trusted management networks.
Enable audit logging on all RTAC devices.
Use certificate-based authentication for RTAC communications.

ICSA-20-205-01.title: GE Digital CIMPLICITY HMI
ICSA-20-205-01.description: A vulnerability in GE CIMPLICITY HMI allows local code execution through improper input validation. CIMPLICITY is used in power generation and transmission SCADA systems.
recommendations: Update to CIMPLICITY v11.1 or later.
Restrict local logon access to HMI workstations.
Deploy application whitelisting on HMI systems.
Monitor for unauthorized process execution on HMI hosts.
